Discussed channel onramp, integration touchpoints for their managed Kubernetes + edge GPU offering, licensing models (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance needs (SAML, KMS, SOC2), and initial pilot scope/benchmarks. transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-11
- Time: 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Lina (ZenCloud CTO), Marco (Head of Platform), Priya (Cloud Architect)

Summary (auto):
Quick partner intro, understanding ZenCloud Nucleus' channel go-to-market, technical integration surface (onramp agent, VPC peering, tenant isolation), and pilot success criteria.

Topics:
- Channel partnership model and partner incentives
- Technical onramp: agent vs managed connector, network topologies
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for their customers
- Security controls (KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs)
- Pilot scope and benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you taking the time, um, from Redwood side we've got myself, Maya, AE, and Ravi our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Lina: Hi Maya, thanks. I'm Lina, CTO at ZenCloud Nucleus — quick intro, we run a managed k8s across edge colos with optional GPU racks, um, and we're exploring partner onramps.
[00:18] Marco: Marco here, run platform. We're curious about how Redwood would sit in our stack and what work we need to do.
[00:24] Ravi: Awesome, thanks. Quick agenda — partner model, integration touchpoints, security, then pilot framing and next steps. Sound good?
[00:32] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:34] Maya: Great. Lina, could you say a little more about your customers and typical deployment — are they more enterprise regulated, or AI-native startups?
[00:42] Lina: Majority are fintech and telco — so compliance matters. They want private deployments often VPC or even on-prem. Some startups use our hosted offering. We do private KMS integrations for key material.
[00:52] Maya: Okay, good. That aligns with what we've seen — Redwood has hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC/on-prem options. We can map those to a channel offering.
[01:03] Marco: Biggest question: network and tenancy. If we introduce a "Redwood onramp agent" into customer clusters, what data path looks like? Do tokens leave the customer's VPC?
[01:14] Ravi: Good question. For Redwood Private we offer a control plane we can host in your VPC or you can self-host. In that pattern, data stays inside your network; keys can be plugged into customer KMS/HSM. For Hosted API, metadata goes to Redwood, payloads transit — we support TLS and at-rest encryption but enterprise customers often pick Dedicated or Private.
[01:30] Priya: Hmm, okay. You mentioned KMS — do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM integration?
[01:36] Ravi: Yes, we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS out of box; HSM/KMS integrations possible via our Private deployment with KMS connectors. There's sometimes a small additional ops step for HSM.
[01:45] Marco: Can you do SAML/SSO for the console and RBAC for accounts?
[01:49] Maya: Yes SAML SSO and org-level RBAC; we also emit audit logs per token and per-request for compliance.
[01:55] Lina: Security's a must for our customers. We'll need SOC 2 or ISO statements to show them.
[01:59] Maya: We can share SOC 2 Type II and the security whitepaper after the call.
[02:04] Marco: Great. On the technical side, how do you handle large-model KV caches and batching? We have customers with high-concurrency request profiles — how do you avoid tail latency when many small requests hit the model?
[02:16] Ravi: Our runtime does continuous batching and KV cache management; the engine supports optimized kernels and quantization-friendly paths. For Dedicated we can size GPU pools and make sure throughput meets SLOs. There are knobs: batch size, max latency targets, and prefix caching.
[02:31] Priya: Are those knobs exposed via API or is that something we tune with Redwood during pilot?
[02:36] Ravi: Both — there's a tuning API and we provide recommendations via Redwood Optimize. For pilots we usually run experiments to pick batching/caching profiles and quantization that preserve quality.
[02:46] Lina: Another operational question — what happens when capacity is constrained? We need graceful degradation.
[02:51] Maya: We support smart routing and fallbacks — you can set policies to route to lower-cost model variants or to Dedicated fallback pools. Also region fallback if a region is down.
[03:02] Marco: Good. Pricing — do partners get reseller margins or referral fees? What's the partner financial model?
[03:08] Maya: For channel partners we have a two-track program: referral (one-time credit or percentage of first-year usage) and reseller (margin on committed Dedicated capacity). We can share partner deck.
[03:18] Priya: For the pilot, we want to run an apples-to-apples benchmark of a few common models — say 8k and 32k context sizes, and a mix of short chat vs long generation.
[03:28] Ravi: We can run that. If you share traces and token distributions we'll reproduce the workload on a Dedicated pool and a Hosted profile and compare latency and cost per token.
[03:36] Priya: We'll do that. Any particular format you need for traces?
[03:39] Ravi: CSV with timestamped request sizes and sequence lengths works; sample rate of 1 in 10 requests is fine to start. We also have a benchmark template I can send.
[03:47] Lina: On legal/compliance — data retention policies, can you configure TTLs or auto-delete?
[03:52] Maya: Yes configurable retention policies per tenant; for Private/Dedicated you can opt for zero-retention or local-only logs. We also integrate with SIEMs for audit streaming.
[04:02] Marco: Any production customers in regulated verticals you can reference?
[04:06] Maya: We have finance and healthcare customers; I can share redacted case studies and an anonymized SOC2 attestation.
[04:13] Priya: From an integration view, what footprint would an onramp agent have on our nodes? We try to keep sidecars minimal.
[04:20] Ravi: The onramp agent is lightweight — typically 50–100MB and a couple of threads for connection pooling. Most customers run it as a daemonset or a dedicated gateway node. For strict environments we can offer an air-gapped package.
[04:31] Marco: Good — and how do you handle billing at the partner level? We have managed tenants and want consolidated billing for accounts we manage.
[04:38] Maya: We support consolidated billing for partners and tenant-level usage breakdown. Also token-level cost reporting to reconcile charges.
[04:46] Lina: Competitors question — we've talked to AetherScale and Aurora Compute, both pitched deep infra control. What would make Redwood the right partner for us?
[04:55] Maya: Two things: production-first developer experience and a unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. That lets you onboard customers fast with predictable economics and fallbacks. Also our Optimize toolkit helps lower unit cost while preserving quality — helpful for cost-sensitive telco workloads.
[05:10] Priya: Latency numbers — do you have ballpark latency for common configs?
[05:14] Ravi: For a Dedicated A100-style pool with optimized kernels you'd see single-turn latencies in the 60–150ms range for short responses, depending on model. For longer sequences and 32k context it scales but we manage KV cache to reduce repeated prefix. Hosted profiles vary more. We'll share example spreadsheets.
[05:32] Marco: Is there an option for partial offload — keep embeddings local but generation in Redwood hosted — hybrid routing?
[05:39] Ravi: Yep, smart routing policies allow splitting by route, model type, or tenant. You can keep embeddings in your on-prem cluster and route generation to our hosted endpoint if needed.
[05:48] Lina: For pilot success criteria — what would you consider a good pilot?
[05:52] Maya: Demonstrated parity on quality with acceptable latency envelope, and a predictable cost per 1M tokens that maps to customer SLAs. Also integration sanity — SSO, KMS, and billing flow validated.
[06:04] Priya: OK. Timeline — we want a thin pilot in 4–6 weeks if we can move quickly.
[06:09] Maya: That's reasonable. Typical pilot is 4 weeks: integration, run benchmark, review results, then expand.
[06:14] Marco: Any significant engineering lift on our side? We want to avoid long projects for customers.
[06:19] Ravi: Minimal. For Private you need to provision the control plane in your VPC and configure KMS. For reseller model we can do much of the heavy lifting. We'll give a checklist.
[06:30] Priya: Network egress costs are a concern for some customers. If traffic leaves the VPC for Hosted, who absorbs that?
[06:36] Maya: Usually customers budget for egress; for Dedicated/Private egress stays inside your cloud or your peering so it's minimized. We can discuss bloom policies for routing to lower-egress regions.
[06:46] Lina: Are there any red flags — compatibility issues we've hit with SI partners historically?
[06:50] Ravi: The common gotchas are kernel mismatches for optimized GPU drivers and mismatched libc versions in on-prem. We provide recommended AMIs and a preflight script to validate nodes.
[07:01] Marco: Good to know. Priya, anything else on the tech side?
[07:05] Priya: One thing — observability: do you expose per-request traces so we can integrate with our distributed tracing?
[07:11] Ravi: Yes, we emit request-level traces and can hook into OpenTelemetry collectors. There's a tracing SDK and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console.
[07:20] Maya: Okay, sounds like we're aligned on next steps. I'll circulate the partner one-pager and the pricing tracks. Ravi will send the benchmark template and sample spreadsheets. Priya/Marco will send workload traces.
[07:31] Lina: Sounds good. Also, can you include a slide on our joint go-to-market — co-branded webinar or joint case study — that's something we want to explore.
[07:40] Maya: Absolutely, we can include partner GTM options in the deck.
[07:44] Marco: Let's pick a date for the deep dive — week of 2026-02-23 works for us.
[07:49] Maya: Great. Ravi, can you lead that?
[07:52] Ravi: Yep, happy to. I'll prepare a deep dive focusing on benchmarking methodology and Private deployment steps.
[07:58] Priya: Quick question — do you support model pinning and version rollouts? We want canary deploys to avoid regressions.
[08:05] Ravi: Yes, rollouts, pinning, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies are in the platform.
[08:11] Lina: Excellent. Anything else?
[08:14] Maya: If not, we'll wrap. Thanks everyone for time. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[08:20] Marco: Thanks.
[08:22] Priya: Thanks all.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions for acronyms (K-V cash instead of KV cache, V-P-C spelled out), some overlap when multiple people speak.

End of meeting.
